official.deadline_note: Annual call: applications are accepted online only from 10 April to 30 September each year; the 2026 call closed on 30 September 2026, so the next deadline is 30 September 2027. Results are announced in December and the accepted exchange must start by May of the following year.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle - call for applications 10 April to 30 September; review October-November; results announced in December; exchange to start by May Y+1
official.status_note: The online application form is submitted exclusively during the annual window of 10 April to 30 September; the 2026 window closed on 30 September 2026 and the next call opens on 10 April 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The official pages state the HFA provides financial support of up to EUR 2,500 per month to the grant recipient, in addition to the agreement to be arranged with the selected host institution; they publish no tuition provision.
benefits: EUR 2,500 per month with a maximum of EUR 10,000 according to the length of the project
Paid in tranches: 25% three weeks before the starting date, 40% six weeks after, 25% twelve weeks after, and the remaining 10% once the training report has been provided to the HFA
A fixed-term contract of employment is usually signed between the host institution and the grant recipient
Recipients are encouraged to submit an abstract to the Heart Failure Congress and may present their project on the HFA stage together with their supervisor
eligibility: Be under 40 years old at the day of the application deadline
Be an HFA Member, or Fellow of the HFA

Hold an MD but not yet a post defined as 'permanent', 'senior staff' or 'consultant', and demonstrate expertise in heart failure through examination, practice, scientific publication in a relevant journal, or abstract presentation at a national or international meeting; OR
Hold a PhD, DPhil degree or equivalent, or have submitted a thesis before starting the research period relating to the grant
Project undertaken in a suitable university department or institution in an ESC member country outside the applicant's own country, preferably at an HFA ICARe-HF Accredited Centre
requirements: Active HFA membership or Fellowship as of the application deadline
Application and project proposal prepared in collaboration with the proposed host centre, which must nominate a supervisor
Signed approval of the host institution obtained before submitting the application
Submission exclusively online through a My ESC account during the application period
All supporting documents returned and uploaded with the application in time for the closing date
documents: CV covering postgraduate career and present employment, previous training in clinical cardiology, research experience, academic record, and publications in refereed journals with journal titles, page numbers and co-author names
Document to be completed by the current head of department or supervisor
Project description prepared jointly with the proposed supervisor
Document to be completed by the future supervisor at the host centre
Letter of recommendation (e.g. from the head of department or supervisor)
selection_criteria: Feasibility and importance of the project, with assessment of sustained benefits for local and global cardiovascular disease reduction - 50%
Candidate's profile: optimal career stage and achievements so far - 20%
Citizenship or permanent residence in a low- or middle-income country as defined by the World Bank - 20%
Quality of the host centre in the research or training field and its track record or expertise in the topic of the application - 10%
coverage: Financial support up to EUR 2,500 per month with a maximum of EUR 10,000 to the grant recipient, according to the length of the project
Paid directly to the grant recipient in four tranches over the exchange period
The ESC will not provide assistance with transfer or household removal expenses incurred on taking up an award
application_method: Log in to the applications section of your My ESC account, click 'New Grant Application' and then 'Apply now' next to the HFA grants programme form
The application form is visible and accessible only during the application period and only if the eligibility criteria are fulfilled
Applications are considered by an HFA-composed Task Force within 10 weeks
official.application_route: Apply online exclusively through your My ESC account during the annual 10 April - 30 September window, after securing acceptance and signed approval from the host centre.
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality or residency restriction is published for applying; the host centre must be in an ESC member country other than the applicant's own, and 20% of the score is reserved for applicants with citizenship or permanent residence in a World Bank low- or middle-income country.
official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants of any nationality who are HFA members or Fellows; cross-border mobility is mandatory, since the project must take place outside the applicant's own country.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Specialised heart failure research or training in a basic, translational or clinical topic, at a centre whose track record or expertise matches the subject of the application, preferably an HFA ICARe-HF Accredited Centre.
official.research_requirement: A personally composed proposal for specialised heart failure research or training, prepared jointly with the proposed supervisor, for a project lasting three to 12 months.
official.duration: Any period from three to 12 months as requested by the applicant
official.description: The HFA grants programme enables young heart failure investigators and clinicals to undertake specialised heart failure research or training in an ESC member country outside their own country, preferably at an HFA ICARe-HF Accredited Centre, with financial support of up to EUR 2,500 per month (maximum EUR 10,000).
official.program_type: Professional association research and training grant with mandatory international mobility

verification.notes: Amount (EUR 2,500 per month, maximum EUR 10,000), the annual 10 April - 30 September window, payment tranches, eligibility, documents and selection weightings were all confirmed on escardio.org; the ESC publishes no English-language test score and leaves language requirements to the host centre.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a mobility stipend, not a salary or a full award: the HFA pays up to EUR 2,500 a month, capped at EUR 10,000, for a three to twelve-month heart failure research or training stay at a centre in another ESC member country. Cash arrives in four tranches and the final 10% is withheld until you file your training report, so early cash flow depends on the host arrangements being settled well before departure. Applications are only possible inside the annual 10 April to 30 September window and only once your host supervisor and head of department have signed off, which means the real preparation happens months before the form even opens. Scoring is dominated by the project itself, as feasibility and impact carry half the marks.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Cardiologists and early-career heart failure researchers under 40 who already hold HFA membership and can secure a willing host supervisor abroad for a focused three to twelve-month project.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm active HFA membership or Fellowship well before 10 April, since the online form is only visible to applicants who meet the eligibility criteria
Contact a host centre early and obtain signed approval from its head of department on the ESC template; the regulations call this the key task before applying
Agree project scope and exchange dates with the host supervisor so the stay fits the three to twelve-month window and can start by May of the following year
Build the CV with journal titles, page numbers and co-author names for every publication, rather than a bare reference list
Check that your My ESC account profile details, including membership status and date of birth, are accurate, because an out-of-date record can hide the application form
Read the full conditions and regulations before drafting, especially the clauses on insurance, extra earnings, holidays and early termination
common_rejection_risks: A proposal that reads as a general interest in heart failure rather than a feasible, time-boxed project with a named host supervisor and facilities
A host centre whose profile does not match the topic, when host quality and track record are explicitly scored and ICARe-HF Accredited Centres are preferred
Missing or unsigned supervisor documents: both the current head of department and the future host supervisor must each complete their own form
Submitting after 30 September or expecting a late-summer decision, when review runs October to November and results land in December
An exchange that cannot begin by May of the following year, which forfeits the award
Overlooking the 20% weighting for World Bank low- or middle-income country citizenship or permanent residence and self-eliminating without checking residency status
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The ESC explicitly does not assist with transfer or household removal expenses, and the stipend is capped at EUR 10,000 regardless of actual living costs at the host location, so budget separately for relocation, personal and professional insurance, local taxes, visa and admin costs, and any project expenditure beyond the cap that the regulations expect you to settle with the host department in advance.
document_audit: The CV has content requirements, not just a format: postgraduate career, current employment, clinical cardiology training, research experience, academic record and full publication details
Two distinct supervisor documents exist, one for the current head of department and one for the future host supervisor, and confusing or swapping them is a common slip
The project description must be prepared jointly with the host supervisor, so circulate the ESC template to them early rather than drafting it alone
The recommendation letter is free-form but should come from a head of department or supervisor able to vouch for both you and the project
The application form is hidden outside the window and to ineligible profiles, so verify access in August rather than in the final week
alerts: Applications open 10 April and close 30 September; there is no rolling or late submission route

The final 10% of the grant is released only after the training report reaches the HFA, and the HFA can withhold funding or demand repayment if the exchange ends early, which must be reported without undue delay
No private practice is allowed, any outside earnings during working hours must be reported, and only up to six hours a week of approved teaching or clinical work is exempt
Every publication arising from the work must carry the exact HFA acknowledgement sentence and a print-off must be sent to the HFA
Additional grants are permitted but must be reconciled against the EUR 10,000 HFA maximum
Language requirements are set by the host centre rather than the ESC, so confirm what the supervisor expects before accepting an offer
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure host acceptance and the signed templates during spring and summer, submit the online form in your My ESC account before 30 September, then an HFA task force scores it within about 10 weeks with results in December and a mandatory start by May.
